results.evidence: The route's own page lists it as 320 ft (97 m), 3 pitches, matching length_m 98. The 65 m first pitch is a traverse behind the falls (spray cone) rather than vertical gain, and the waterfall itself is about 286 ft (87 m) high, so the 143 m of rope-length is not total height.

Route page lists 800 ft (242 m), 3 pitches and says that after the 20 m pitch 3 the party unroped and climbed about 500 ft of steep snow in Center Chute plus a short AI2/3 section to the ridge. The 115 m of roped pitches plus the unroped couloir accounts for the stated total. Searches for a second page found nothing independent, but no change is needed.

The route page (closed for cultural resource protection, no descent text) lists the route as 100 ft (30 m), matching length_m 30, so a 60 ft lower/rappel cannot reach the ground from the top. The 60 ft figure is the outlier and is removed. Searched the web for the name; only the area page and route page exist.

The route page lists Bandito Route as Aid, 40 ft (12 m), a bolt ladder through the cap-rock roof to the summit, matching length_m 12; the visitutah page also calls it a bolted clip-up aid climb. No source states the summit rappel length. An 80 ft rappel could be the full drop from the summit to the base of the cap, which is longer than the roof climb, so I cannot prove it wrong. Searched mountainproject, summitpost, visitutah, roadtripryan.

The aid route page (5.8 C1, Trad Aid) says this is the aided ascent of the same buttress as the free route; the Mountaineers and classic-climbs references give the aid version as 5.9 C1/A1. So the free-line overview is wrong for this row. The overview wording is replaced. Pitch count found 10 on one page and 11 on another, so pitches 0 (impossible) is blanked.

results.evidence: Route page lists 600 ft (182 m), 4 pitches, and says the descent is double-rope raps back down the route (a comment says three). With two 60 m ropes each rappel is up to about 60 m, so four rappels cover 183 m; 'doubled ropes' means a two-rope system, and rope_length_m is the length of a single rope. A summit-post note also mentions a single 70 m rope as an option.

results.evidence: Route page lists 850 ft, 7 pitches and combines the ridge section as 'P6 & 7' (one long simul-climbed pitch of about 60 m); a separate trip report also calls it 850 ft, 7 pitch. The overview's 'P6-7' is one pitch, so the opening 'Eight pitches' should be seven.

A 1982 account describes the couloir as about 300 ft of ice ribbon, 300 ft of lower-angle ice and 100 ft more, ending about 100 ft below the Enclosure summit, i.e. roughly 700 ft (about 213 m). The stored 2134 m matches a '7000 ft' header on the route page that is plainly a typo for 700 ft, and is impossible for a 3-pitch couloir. Blanked since the exact figure (route page vs account, route including Valhalla traverse) is not stated by two sources.
